meaning: to pour; to reverse, back up; to turn upside down

senses.en: to pour; to tip out (倒水 'pour water', 倒茶 'pour tea')
to reverse, move backwards (倒车 'reverse a car')
to turn upside down or the wrong way round

examples.en: Let me pour you a glass of water.
examples.analysis: 倒 is 'to pour' (dào, fourth tone). 给你 + 倒 = 'pour for you': the person who benefits comes before the verb with 给. 倒杯水 drops 一 before the measure word 杯, as speech often does. 吧 turns it into a friendly offer.

examples.zh: 水太多了，倒一点儿出来。
examples.en: That's too much water. Pour a little out.
examples.analysis: 倒 + amount + 出来 = 'pour some out'. The amount 一点儿 'a little' sits between the verb and the direction word 出来 'out'. There is no subject because it is an instruction to the person holding the glass or the pot.

examples.en: Back up a bit more… OK, stop!
examples.analysis: Here 倒 means 'to reverse, back up', as when guiding a driver into a parking space. 往后 'towards the back' gives the direction; 再 'more' and 一点儿 'a little' give the amount. The car is understood; the full phrase is 倒车 'reverse the car'.

related.en: to fall over; to change (buses, trains): a separate entry, third tone. Note 倒车 is read dào chē 'reverse' but dǎo chē 'change buses'

meaning: to divide, split; to hand out; to tell apart

senses.en: to divide, split into parts or groups (分成两组 'split into two groups')
to hand out, distribute (分给大家 'hand out to everyone')
to tell apart, distinguish (分不出来 'can't tell apart')

examples.zh: 水果我已经分给大家了。
examples.en: I've already handed out the fruit to everyone.
examples.analysis: 分 + 给 + people = 'hand out to them'. The fruit is named first as the topic, then 我 + 已经 'already' + the verb. 了 at the end marks the job as done.

examples.en: Let's split into two groups.
examples.analysis: 分 + 成 + result: 分成两组 'divide into two groups'. 成 'into' names what you end up with. 两, not 二, goes before a counted noun such as 组. 吧 makes it a suggestion.

examples.zh: 他们两个人太像了，我分不出来。
examples.en: The two of them look so alike that I can't tell them apart.
examples.analysis: Here 分 means 'to tell apart'. 分不出来 = verb + 不 + result: 'can't manage to tell apart'; the positive is 分得出来. 太像了 'so alike' gives the reason first, then the result.

related.en: minute; cent; point (score): the noun and measure-word entry

meaning: to complete, finish (a task, a piece of work)

senses.en: to complete, finish (work, homework, a task)
to achieve, fulfill (a goal, a plan)

examples.zh: 这个月的工作都完成了吗？
examples.en: Is all of this month's work done?
examples.analysis: 完成 + 了 = 'has been completed'. The work is the subject and no doer is named: Chinese often starts with the thing done. 都 'all' covers every part of the work; 吗 asks yes or no.

examples.en: I haven't finished my homework yet.
examples.analysis: 还没 + verb + 呢 = 'not yet'. The negative of 完成了 is 没完成, with no 了. 作业 'homework' comes first as the topic; 呢 marks the situation as still going on.

examples.zh: 这么多事，我一个人完成不了。
examples.en: With this much to do, I can't finish it all by myself.
examples.analysis: Verb + 不了 = 'cannot manage to': 完成不了 says the job is too big. 一个人 'one person' here means 'on my own'. Mind the reading: 了 is liǎo in this pattern, not le.

related.en: to finish; to be used up (做完, 吃完)
to finish doing; more casual than 完成 (写完, 吃完)

meaning: won't do, not allowed; doesn't work; no good (at)

senses.en: won't do; not allowed (refusing or ruling something out)
no good; doesn't work (a plan, a machine, someone's skill)

examples.en: Tomorrow's no good. What about the day after?
examples.analysis: 不行 rules out a time: 'tomorrow won't work'. It is the whole predicate, with no other verb. 后天呢？ = 'what about the day after tomorrow?': a noun + 呢 offers an alternative.

examples.en: No, you can't go by yourself.
examples.analysis: Said alone at the start, 不行 is a firm 'no' to a request or plan. The next clause spells out what is ruled out: 不能 'can't, isn't allowed to'. From a parent or a boss it closes the matter; between equals it can sound blunt.

examples.en: I'm no good at singing. You sing.
examples.analysis: Activity + 不行 = 'bad at it'. 我唱歌 'my singing' is the topic and 不行 judges it. 你唱吧 passes the turn to the other person.

collocations.en: can't go on; (of a thing) has had it

meaning: look, appearance; style (of clothes); the way things are

senses.en: look, appearance (how a person or thing seems)
style, cut, shape (of clothes or objects)
the way things are (老样子 'same as ever')

examples.zh: 看你的样子，昨天没睡好吧？
examples.en: From the look of you, you didn't sleep well last night, did you?
examples.analysis: 看你的样子 = 'judging by how you look'. 样子 is the visible look of a person. 吧 at the end turns the guess into 'right?', expecting a yes. 睡好 = 'sleep well', with 好 as the result.

examples.zh: 这件衣服样子不错，可是颜色我不喜欢。
examples.en: The style of this piece of clothing is nice, but I don't like the color.
examples.analysis: For clothes, 样子 is the style or cut, as opposed to the color. 这件衣服 is the topic and 样子不错 comments on it: 'this piece of clothing, the style is nice'. 可是 'but' brings in the drawback; after it, 颜色 also comes first as the topic: 'the color, I don't like'.

examples.zh: 他还是以前的样子，一点儿也没变。
examples.en: He looks just the way he used to. He hasn't changed a bit.
examples.analysis: 以前的样子 = 'the way he was before': 的 links the time word to 样子. 还是 'still'. 一点儿也没变 = 'hasn't changed at all': 一点儿 + 也 + negative verb = 'not even a little'.

meaning: to carry (by a handle); to mention, bring up; to raise

senses.en: to carry something hanging from the hand (a bag, a bucket)
to mention, bring up (a topic)
to raise, put forward (a question, an idea, a request)

examples.zh: 东西太多了，我帮你提吧。
examples.en: That's a lot of stuff. Let me carry it for you.
examples.analysis: 提 is carrying by a handle, with the load hanging from the hand: shopping bags, a suitcase, a kettle. 帮你 + verb = 'do it for you'. 吧 makes the offer friendly.

examples.en: Don't bring that up again.
examples.analysis: Here 提 means 'to mention, bring up'. 别再 + verb + 了 = 'don't do it any more'. 那件事 'that matter': 件 is the measure word for matters and events. Said when a topic is painful or embarrassing.

examples.en: Feel free to raise any questions you have.
examples.analysis: 提 + question or idea = 'raise, put forward'. 什么 + 都 = 'any at all', so this is not a question. 可以 'may' invites people to speak, as at the end of a meeting or a class.

collocations.en: don't even mention it (it was awful)

meaning: part; portion; section

senses.en: part, portion, section (of a whole: a text, a job, a group)

measure.note: 这个部分 'this part'; 这部分, with no 个, is also common

examples.en: I don't quite understand this part.
examples.analysis: 部分 is a section of something larger: a lesson, a report, a form. 这个部分 comes first as the topic, then the comment. 不太 + verb = 'not quite', softer than plain 不.

examples.en: Which part do you find the hardest?
examples.analysis: 哪 + 个 + 部分 = 'which part'. 觉得 'feel, find' asks for an opinion. 最 + adjective = 'the most': 最难 'hardest'. A teacher or a colleague might ask this after a task.

examples.en: I'll do this part of the work.
examples.analysis: 部分 + noun = 'part of the…': 这部分工作 'this part of the work', with no 的 and no measure word. 我来 + verb volunteers the speaker: 'let me do it'. 来 here does not mean 'come'.

meaning: to require, ask (someone to do something); a requirement, request

senses.en: to require, ask (someone to do something)
requirement, request; what someone expects

measure.note: 一个要求 'a request'; in formal lists 点: 两点要求

examples.en: The company requires us to arrive at eight.
examples.analysis: 要求 + person + action = 'require someone to do something'. 我们 is the object of 要求 and also the one who does 到 'arrive'. Rules from an employer, a school or a doctor fit this verb.

examples.en: What are you looking for in a place to live?
examples.analysis: Here 要求 is a noun: 'requirements, what you want'. 对 + thing + 有要求 = 'have requirements for something'. A rental agent might ask this before showing you apartments.

examples.en: I don't have any other requests.
examples.analysis: 要求 is a noun again, after 没有 'have no'. 别的 'other' goes straight before it. Said at the end of a list of wishes, or to show you are easy to please.

related.en: to let; to have someone do something

meaning: although; even though

senses.en: although, even though; the next clause usually has 但是, 可是, 却 or 还是

examples.zh: 虽然有点儿贵，但是很好吃。
examples.en: It's a bit pricey, but it's really good.
examples.analysis: 虽然 opens the clause that concedes a point; 但是 'but' brings in the main point. English picks 'although' or 'but'; Chinese commonly uses both together, as here. 有点儿 + adjective marks a mild complaint.

examples.zh: 我虽然学过，可是都忘了。
examples.en: I did learn it, but I've forgotten all of it.
examples.analysis: 虽然 can come after the subject: 我虽然… 'I, although…'. 学过 = 'have studied it at some point', with 过 marking past experience. 可是 is a spoken alternative to 但是. 都忘了 'forgotten it all'.

examples.zh: 虽然是周末，他还是不休息。
examples.en: Even though it's the weekend, he still doesn't take a break.
examples.analysis: Here the second half has no 但是; 还是 'still, all the same' carries the contrast instead. 是周末 'it is the weekend' needs no subject. 不休息 'doesn't take a break' says what he chooses to do.

meaning: to handle, sort out (a matter); to get (a card, a document) done

senses.en: to handle, deal with, take care of (a matter, an errand)
to apply for and get (a card, a passport): 办卡 'get a card'
to hold, run (an event, a business)

examples.zh: 我出去办个事，马上回来。
examples.en: I'm heading out to take care of something. I'll be right back.
examples.analysis: 办事 = 'take care of a matter, run an errand', with 个 slipped in to make it sound small and quick. 出去 + 办 = 'go out and do'. 马上回来 'back right away' is the usual follow-up.

examples.en: I'd like to go to the bank and get a card.
examples.analysis: 办 + document = 'apply for and get': 办卡 'get a (bank) card', 办护照 'get a passport'. The verb covers the whole process, from applying to holding the card. 想去 + place + verb = 'want to go there and do it'. No measure word is needed when you just name the thing.

examples.en: How's that matter coming along?
examples.analysis: Verb + 得 + 怎么样 asks how well something is going: 办得怎么样 'how is the handling going'. 了 adds 'by now'. 那件事 is the topic, a matter both people already know about.

collocations.en: to run errands; to get things done

related.en: what should we do? (its own entry)

meaning: to think of; to expect (often 没想到 'didn't expect')

senses.en: to think of, come up with (an idea, a person, a solution)
to expect, foresee (mostly in 没想到 'didn't expect')

examples.en: I didn't expect you to be here too!
examples.analysis: 没想到 = 'didn't expect': a common way to voice surprise. What was unexpected follows as a whole clause, 你也在这儿 'you are here too'. 没 negates it because the expecting did not happen.

examples.en: I've thought of a good way to do it!
examples.analysis: 想到 + thing = 'think of, come up with'. 到 shows the thinking reached a result; 想办法 without 到 means 'try to find a way'. 了 after the verb marks it as done.

examples.en: How did you think of that?
examples.analysis: 是…的 frames something that already happened and asks about one detail, here 怎么 'how'. 想到 has no object: 'it' (the idea) is understood. Often said with admiration.

related.en: to think; to want; to miss

meaning: to add; plus; to increase

senses.en: to add, put in more (加菜 'order more dishes')
plus (in sums: 三加四 'three plus four')
to increase, raise (加钱 'pay more')

examples.en: Let's order two more dishes.
examples.analysis: 加 = 'add more': 加菜 is what you say when ordering extra dishes at a restaurant. 再 'more' + 加 + number + measure word + noun. 吧 makes it a suggestion to the table.

examples.en: What's eight plus five?
examples.analysis: In sums 加 is 'plus', between the numbers as in English. 是多少 'is how much' asks for the answer; 等于多少 'equals how much' is the more formal version, common in class.

examples.en: Don't add any more. That's enough already.
examples.analysis: 别 + verb + 了 = 'stop doing it', said while someone keeps adding things: sugar to your cup, hot water to the pot, dishes to the order. 已经…了 'already': 够 'enough' has been reached.

meaning: face

senses.en: face
face, self-respect (丢脸 'lose face')

measure.note: 一张脸 'a face'; 张 is for flat surfaces

examples.en: Why has your face gone red?
examples.analysis: 你脸 'your face' without 的 is normal in speech for body parts. 怎么 + adjective + 了 asks 'how come it has become…?'; 了 marks the change. Said to someone who is blushing or flushed.

examples.en: I'm going to wash my face.
examples.analysis: 洗脸 'wash one's face' with 个 slipped in: 洗个脸. Verb + 个 + object makes it sound quick and casual. 去 + verb = 'go and do it'.

examples.zh: 一看他的脸就知道他不高兴。
examples.en: One look at his face and you can tell he's unhappy.
examples.analysis: 一 + verb … 就 … = 'as soon as …, at once …': 一看他的脸 'one look at his face'. 他的脸 keeps 的 here. 知道 has no stated subject: it means 'you can tell'.

meaning: different; not the same

senses.en: different, not the same (A 跟 B 不同)
various, different kinds of (不同的 + noun)

examples.en: What's the difference between these two?
examples.analysis: 有什么不同 = 'what difference is there'. Here 不同 works like a noun, 'a difference', after 有. 这两个 'these two' is the topic. When comparing two products, 有什么区别 or 有什么不一样 is just as common in everyday speech.

examples.en: This time is different from last time.
examples.analysis: A 跟 B 不同 = 'A is different from B'; 跟 'with, from' brings in what is compared. In casual talk 不一样 says the same thing and is more common; 不同 sounds a little more careful.

examples.zh: 不同的人有不同的想法。
examples.en: Different people have different ideas.
examples.analysis: Before a noun, 不同 + 的 = 'different (kinds of)'. The pattern 不同的 X 有不同的 Y is a common way to say things vary from person to person. 想法 = 'idea, way of thinking'.

related.en: different; the everyday way to say it

meaning: family (as a unit); household

senses.en: family as a unit, household (parents, children, home life)

measure.note: 一个家庭 'a family'; official counts use 户

examples.zh: 现在很多家庭只有一个孩子。
examples.en: These days many families have only one child.
examples.analysis: 家庭 is the family as a unit or household, the word for counting or describing families. 很多 + noun needs no measure word. 只有 'only have'. For 'my family' in daily talk, people usually say 我家.

examples.zh: 家庭和工作，哪个更重要？
examples.en: Family or work: which matters more?
examples.analysis: Two nouns joined by 和 are set up as the topic, then the question: 哪个更重要 'which is more important'. 更 'more' compares them. Here 家庭 means family life as a whole.

examples.zh: 我们家是一个很普通的家庭。
examples.en: We're a pretty ordinary family.
examples.analysis: 我们家 'our family' is the everyday way to refer to your own family; 家庭 then classifies it as a type: 一个很普通的家庭 'a very ordinary family'. Description + 的 + 家庭 says what kind of family. Common when people talk about their background.

meaning: to pretend; to install; to pack, hold (in a container)

senses.en: to pretend, put on an act (装没看见 'pretend not to see')
to install, fit (a door, a light, an app)
to pack, load; to hold (装不下 'won't fit')

examples.en: Stop pretending. I know it was you.
examples.analysis: 装 alone = 'to pretend, put on an act'. 别 + verb + 了 = 'stop doing it'. What is being faked is clear from the situation, so 装 needs no object. Said when you have seen through someone's act: teasing between friends, sharp if you are annoyed.

examples.en: Was this door just put in?
examples.analysis: Here 装 means 'to install, fit': doors, lights, air conditioners, apps. 是…的 describes how the door came to be; 新 before the verb means 'newly'. 吗 asks yes or no.

examples.en: This bag is too small. It won't all fit.
examples.analysis: 装 = 'to put into a container, hold'. 装不下 = verb + 不 + 下: 'can't fit it in'; the positive is 装得下 'it fits'. The things to be packed are understood.

meaning: to check, examine; an examination, (medical) test

senses.en: to check, inspect (work, luggage, a room)
to examine (a patient): 检查身体 'have a check-up'
examination; (medical) test

measure.note: 做一次检查 'have an examination'; casually 做个检查, with a light 个

examples.en: When you've finished writing, check it over.
examples.analysis: 检查 + 一下儿 = 'give it a check'; 一下儿 makes the request light. 写完了再… = 'finish writing, then…': 再 here means 'then, after that', not 'again'.

examples.en: The doctor says I need to get checked out.
examples.analysis: Here 检查 is a noun, 'examination, test': 做 + (一)个 + 检查 = 'have an exam done'. 要 = 'need to'. The 'I' is left out; context makes clear who will be examined.

examples.en: Are the test results back yet?
examples.analysis: 检查 goes straight before 结果 with no 的: 检查结果 'test results'. 出来了 'have come out', with 了 marking the change. 吗 asks yes or no.

related.en: to look at; (看病) to see a doctor

meaning: excuse me; sorry; embarrassed, too shy (to do something)

senses.en: excuse me; sorry (for a small trouble)
embarrassed; too shy (to do something)

examples.en: Sorry I'm late.
examples.analysis: 不好意思 is the everyday light apology for a small trouble you caused. 来晚了 = 'came late': 晚 is the result of 来, and 了 marks it as done. For bigger faults, 对不起 is the usual choice.

examples.zh: 不好意思，洗手间在哪儿？
examples.en: Excuse me, where's the restroom?
examples.analysis: Here 不好意思 works like 'excuse me' before a question to a stranger, staff or a colleague. It shows you know you are interrupting. The question that follows is a plain 在哪儿 'where is'.

examples.en: He feels too awkward to ask the teacher.
examples.analysis: 不好意思 + verb = 'feel too awkward or shy to do it'. It sits before the verb, as 想 'want to' would. The sentence describes his feeling, which is what keeps him from asking.

meaning: medicine; drug

senses.en: medicine, drug (pills, syrup, ointment)

examples.en: The medicine's on the table. Remember to take it.
examples.analysis: 药 is the subject: 药在桌子上 'the medicine is on the table'. 记得 + verb = 'remember to'. The object of 吃 is dropped because 药 has just been mentioned. Chinese 'eats' medicine: 吃药 = 'take medicine'.

examples.en: Take this medicine three times a day.
examples.analysis: Dosage order: medicine + 一天 'per day' + 吃 + 三次 'three times'. The number of times comes after the verb. 这个药 is the topic, and 'you' is left out.

examples.zh: 我不想吃药，喝一点儿热水就好了。
examples.en: I don't want to take medicine. A little hot water and I'll be fine.
examples.analysis: 药 is the object of 吃, and 不想 'don't want to' refuses it. 喝一点儿热水就好了 = 'drink a little hot water and it will be fine': 就好了 'then it will be fine'. A familiar line in Chinese homes.

meaning: music

senses.en: music

measure.note: 一段音乐 'a piece of music'; usually uncounted: 听音乐

examples.en: What kind of music do you like?
examples.analysis: 音乐 is the object of 听 'listen to', and 喜欢 + 听音乐 = 'like listening to music'. 什么 + noun = 'what kind of'. A standard small-talk question.

examples.zh: 我开车的时候喜欢听音乐。
examples.en: I like listening to music when I drive.
examples.analysis: 听音乐 'listening to music' is what the speaker likes. The time clause 我开车的时候 'when I drive' normally comes before the main verb; English can put 'when…' at the end, Chinese usually puts it first.

examples.en: Stop listening to music and go to sleep!
examples.analysis: 别 + verb + object + 了 = 'stop doing it': 别听音乐了. 快 + verb urges 'hurry up and…'. A parent's line at bedtime.
